column3: Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “of it.”
“Who had a creditor” is rendered “who was in debt,” and “bitter of soul” as “discontented.”
“Go out with you” is rendered “come and stay with you.”
“He led them” is rendered “he left them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“At the high place” (often read “on the height”) is rendered “on the height.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Opens my ear” is rendered “discloses to me,” and “feeling pain on me” as “is sorry for me.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Food” is rendered “provisions.”
NASB supplies “someone” as the one sent.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Turns aside to your bodyguard” is rendered “who is captain over your guard”; the meaning is uncertain.
“Put anything against” is rendered “impute anything to,” and “anything small or great” as “nothing at all of this whole affair.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Runners” is rendered “guards,” and “uncovered my ear” as “reveal it to me.”
“Fall on” is rendered “attack,” and “carried an ephod” as “wore the linen ephod.”
Close to the Hebrew; “suckling child” is rendered “infants.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“I have turned in every life” is rendered “I have brought about the death of every person”; the Hebrew is difficult.
“You are in good care with me” is rendered “you are safe with me.”
